questions.question: What will Amazon Web Services’ reported revenue be for fiscal year 2026?
questions.why_it_matters: AWS is a major Amazon business and a stated driver of the article’s growth outlook. Its full-year revenue would show whether cloud momentum is translating into a material business result; it is distinct from Amazon’s total revenue and from the existing question about Google Cloud revenue.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing questions cover combined hyperscaler capital expenditure, compute capacity, and Google Cloud FY2026 revenue, but not AWS revenue. AWS’s revenue can change independently of those outcomes.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check after Amazon reports FY2026 results, using its earnings release and annual filing for AWS’s reported full-year revenue. The article does not state a reporting date; FY2026 ends December 31, 2026, which is the measurement-period end, not a stated disclosure date.

article:
Market Correction: Social media observers pointed to Amazon shares slipping into a technical correction after an 11% decline from the prior peak. They noted the stock's consolidation phase and upcoming quarterly results slated for late October. Attention centered on position sizing amid the sideways action.
Growth Projections: Commentators referenced expectations for earnings to compound at 24% annually over the next five years. They linked this outlook to accelerating AWS momentum and new AI hardware initiatives. Some highlighted how such expansion could support the current valuation multiple even under conservative assumptions.
Investor Activity: Discussions noted renewed buying interest from several large investors tied to cloud and silicon developments. Participants emphasized the shift away from reliance on external chip suppliers. Overall market chatter reflected measured optimism around these structural tailwinds.
